newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - May 6.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - May 6.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Tuesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
BUSINESS DAY
- Only 40,500 rand out of a possible seven million rand was recovered by the White Commission into irregular public service promotions, a report by the auditor-general has found.

- The Stride committee investigation into Transnet's pension-related debt has recommended that the stocks financing it be cancelled and that all Transnet pensioners be taken over by the state to make the parastatal profitable.
- The world's biggest gold find has been exposed as a hoax, eliciting "shock and dismay" from the Canadian firm that discovered it.

- Mineral and Energy Affairs Minister Penuell Maduna has resurrected the prospect of a government-backed national oil distributor and refiner in a bid to free the market and advance black empowerment efforts.

- Traffic officials accused of issuing up to 300 fraudulent driver's licences a day in the former KwaNdebele homeland allegedly burnt their 1,2 million rand test centre in 1995 to destroy evidence of their activities.
BUSINESS REPORT

- The Stride committee investigating the restructuring of the Transnet pension fund has proposed that the government start paying pensions to existing Transnet pensioners, Transnet managing director Saki Macazoma, said on Monday.
- A bill would be tabled in parliament to regulate privatisation and the restructuring of state assets, Public Enterprises Minister Stella Sigcau said in parliament on Monday.

- Energy Minister Penuell Maduna on Monday launched a scathing attack on multinational oil companies operating in Southern Africa, accusing them of transfer pricing and maintaining a stranglehold on the domestic oil industry.
- LeisureNet, the diversified lifestyles company, is to sell Crawford Education Holdings, its private college subsidiary, to Advanced Technical Systems (AdvTech) in a 180-million rand deal.

- The Maputo Development Corridor received a three billion rand boost on Monday with the signing of a 30-year concession agreement for the construction and maintenance of a toll road between Witbank and the port city.
SAKE-BEELD
- The gold price caught investors at the Johannesburg Stock Exchange unawares on Monday when the price of the yellow metal unexpectedly rose by nearly three dollars per ounce.
- Companies tendering for the management of South Africa's planned national lottery must be heard by March next year.
- Match producer Lion Match is expecting a satisfactory increase in its earnings in the current bookyear.
- Business South Africa has applied for an interdict against Cosatu's mass action campaign which is planned for May 12.
- The state has lost about 700 million rand so far due to thousands of ghost workers in the public service and the unauthorised promotion of others, auditor-general Henri Kluever has found.
THE STAR

- Traffic officials accused of issuing up to 300 fraudulent driver's licences a day in the former homeland of KwaNdebele allegedly burnt their 1,2 million rand test centre in 1995 to destroy all documentary evidence of their activities.

- Zairean President Mobutu Sese Seko's 32-year dictatorship of Zaire is rapidly drawing to an end, but the critical question remaining is whether he stands down peacefully within the next few days or is forced out by rebel leader Laurent Kabila's army.
- The electrified fence on South Africa's northern and eastern borders could soon be switched to "letal mode" to stop illegal immigrants and other cross-border violations.

- Four senior Mpumalanga policemen who, according to earlier testimony from former Vlakplass commander Eugene de Kock, allegedly used dynamite to blow up the mutilated body of ANC activist Sweet Johannes Sambo to prevent "another Steve Biko affair", appeared briefly in the Middelburg Regional Court on Monday.
